Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter
Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of
Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and
look forward to your mark-up.
SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)
Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims
is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.
Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and
only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the
basket is recoverable.
Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after
Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims
unless expressly stated otherwise.
Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same
caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.
Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and
non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.
Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public
registers (see Disclosure Letter).
Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the
Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or
public records.
Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller
will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the
counterparty's written consent.
Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding)
will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.
Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing
bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds
flow.)
Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio
matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.
Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter
and is not expected to be material.
Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course
operating costs.
Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime
above.
Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.
Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and
records are fictional.
1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the
indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including
DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly
searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific
disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent,
payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.
2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause
11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final
written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.
3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2.
As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security
is included.
4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of
every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of
non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject
to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft
Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or
on-costs apply.
6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external
email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity
timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised
person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation
remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no
loss amount.
7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as
a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.
8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each
(AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether
each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale
consent is required merely because shares are sold.
10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of
the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the
Buyer has completed its own verification.
11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer
must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

## Buyer-side assessment

The Seller’s update is not a balanced package for Wattlebridge. It shifts material transaction, disclosure and post-completion risks to the Buyer while proposing restrictions that could make recovery difficult or impossible. This review is based on the update and disclosure letter only; the full SPA, due diligence materials and proposed completion funds flow should be checked before finalising a mark-up.

### Priority pushbacks

1. **Do not let the general warranty cap and time bar govern all claims.**  
   A cap of AUD 4.8 million (20% of the AUD 24 million price), a basket and an 18-month notice period may be negotiable for ordinary warranty claims, but should not apply across the board. Carve out at least:
   - title, ownership and capacity warranties;
   - fraud, deliberate concealment and wilful misconduct;
   - specific indemnities, including Ironquay and any agreed incident, tax or debt indemnities;
   - claims for purchase-price adjustments, completion accounts and debt-free/cash-free shortfalls; and
   - claims arising from unpaid debt or other agreed completion deliverables.

   Title and capacity should have a separate, substantially higher cap—ideally the full purchase price—and a longer limitation period. A general-warranty cap should not quietly become the cap for every remedy.

2. **Reject the blanket “all Claims” limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance wording.**  
   The proposal to apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to “all Claims of any nature” could cut across contractual indemnities, price adjustments, debt repayment obligations and claims for fraud or deliberate concealment. Limit any exclusive-remedy regime to ordinary warranty claims, preserve agreed standalone obligations and remedies, and expressly carve out fraud and wilful misconduct. The Buyer should not waive reliance on information or representations to the extent needed to preserve claims for misrepresentation or deliberate concealment.

3. **Narrow general disclosure and the buyer-knowledge bar.**  
   Disclosure of everything in the data room and public registers—even without identifying what is said to be disclosed—risks turning the entire data room into a blanket qualification of the warranties. Require specific, fair and sufficiently detailed disclosure against the relevant warranty, with documents clearly identified and accessible; reject general disclosure of the whole data room and public records.  
   
   Similarly, limit any knowledge bar to actual knowledge of named Buyer deal-team individuals after reasonable enquiry, if accepted at all. Do not exclude claims for matters merely discoverable in a data room or public records. The Buyer’s access to information is not a substitute for the Seller’s warranties.

4. **Make Bluefen consent a genuine condition to completion.**  
   Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue, and the disclosed change-of-control clause has conditions. The Seller confirms there is no final written consent or evidence those conditions are met. “Reasonable endeavours” and treating the condition as satisfied on delivery of a consent alone are inadequate. Require final, unconditional written consent and satisfaction of all associated conditions before completion, with no material adverse amendment, termination or waiver of Buyer protections. If that cannot be achieved, the Buyer should have a termination right and should not be forced to complete with this risk outstanding.

5. **Require Riverlark debt repayment and security release at or before completion.**  
   The approximately AUD 3.2 million facility remains outstanding and no final discharge is in the data room. A release “following Completion” leaves the Buyer exposed to inherited debt and security over the Company’s assets. Require payoff figures, repayment from completion funds, lender discharge/release documents and evidence of termination of relevant commitments as completion deliverables. Ensure the debt is treated consistently in the debt-free/cash-free mechanics and is not paid twice or left to the Company after completion.

### Other material issues

- **Completion bonuses (DD-005):** AUD 420,000 of conditional completion bonuses are omitted from the draft funds flow. Require the Seller to bear and fund bonuses triggered by the sale or completion, including payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs. Specify the treatment in the funds flow and price mechanics, and prevent double recovery or an undisclosed post-completion liability being left in the Company.

- **Ironquay IP (DD-004 / DD-010):** The Seller’s proposed indemnity for only the SOW3 payment is too narrow. The disclosed contract makes transfer of Project Materials conditional on payment of every SOW3 fee; AUD 180,000 is open, and there is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. Require proof of cleared payment and an effective assignment/transfer of all relevant materials and IP by completion. Obtain warranties and a specific indemnity covering ownership, access, infringement and any resulting remediation or replacement costs—not merely the stated payment.

- **Export/privacy incident (DD-006):** Do not accept the description “preliminary” or “not expected to be material” as a reason to leave the risk unallocated. The disclosure indicates a link went to an unintended external address and may involve about 1,240 personal records, while access, scope and notification obligations remain unknown. Require a completed investigation, preservation of evidence, appropriate containment and any legally required notifications before completion where practicable; ongoing cooperation and prompt notice of developments; and a specific indemnity for incident-related claims, regulatory action, investigation, notification, remediation and response costs. Consider a completion condition or other protection if the position cannot be established.

- **Supplier renewals (DD-008 / DD-011):** AUD 330,000 in related renewals should not be dismissed as ordinary-course costs without understanding timing, scope and termination rights. Obtain the underlying contracts and a schedule of amounts paid, accrued, committed and avoidable. Include accrued or transaction-triggered liabilities in the relevant price mechanics and obtain any needed operating covenant or consent. Do not assume the entire amount is a debt-like item without checking the agreements and accounting treatment.

- **Tax and IP warranties:** The Seller’s assertion that these are “settled” under the general regime is not a substitute for adequate protections. Seek a standalone tax indemnity for pre-completion tax liabilities and robust IP warranties, with appropriate caps, time limits and carve-outs from general thresholds. Check that the relevant warranty and indemnity schedules actually address the identified due diligence risks.

- **Lease and Mossvale:** The disclosure does not establish that landlord consent or Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold. Verify the full contracts and applicable change-of-control provisions; do not convert a mere notification obligation into an unnecessary consent condition, but do require any actual notice, consent or waiver the documents require.

- **Title:** DD-012 is the Seller’s stated source for its assertion that it holds 100% of the shares; it is not a substitute for verification. Confirm the register, constitution, share certificates and any encumbrances or options, and obtain clear title and capacity warranties, transfer documents and any required releases at completion.

## Summary of recommendations

Prioritise the mark-up around **(1)** separating general warranty limits from title, fraud, indemnity and price-adjustment claims; **(2)** rejecting blanket disclosure, knowledge and all-claims remedy restrictions; **(3)** making Bluefen consent and Riverlark repayment/release effective completion protections; and **(4)** resolving bonuses, Ironquay IP and the export incident through clear funds-flow treatment, deliverables and specific protections. Then verify supplier, tax, IP, lease, Mossvale and title matters against the underlying documents. Do not treat the Seller’s characterisations—“ordinary course,” “preliminary” or “adequate”—as conclusions; test them against the contracts, evidence and full SPA.
